I think this is a poor title. The purpose of the article is to debunk wild claims that SSDs will outdo HDDs in every way by the end of 2016.

Until massive SSDs are around the same price as HDDs then I'll agree that it won't be a rout, but if 1 TB drives get even to the $100 pricepoint I'd imagine that adoption numbers would be less linear and more exponential.

That being said, looking at the prices on Newegg the bottom would have to fall out for parity to be achieved. The 500 GB drives would need to lose around $100, and the 1 TB drives would need to lose over $200. Steep as those drops are, I can see it being possible over the course of 18 months. If/when that does happen, then I can easily see HDDs being relegated to NAS. Even if that's the case, I would love to get my hands on some 2 - 4 TB NAS drives for around $50/each.

They'll still be around, but they'll probably leave the consumer market and be relegated to NAS and archival applications. Profit margins are tiny on current HDDs to keep people buying them, and fewer and fewer are. OEMs are putting SSDs in laptops and now even in desktops for mainstream configurations more and more as the user experience is many times better with an SSD.

There are even full size 14-15 inch laptops on the market that don't even offer a hard drive version since it'd be waste on a higher end system. Not to mention, in the server/NAS usage setting you don't always just need storage/$, depending on the application there could be a variety of other performance factors involved such as latency, random access speed, and active idle power efficiency (disks spinning in the case of the hard drive) and for all of these metric SSDs can and often do destroy HDDs.
